purpose: Which changed paths make a pull request subject to MASTER_EXECUTION_ROADMAP.md §G.2's first row, which reads: "Any `engine/` security code (wall · leases · gates · signatures · control-plane · root model)" -- Builder on its "own audited branch", Architect audit "mandatory", Owner approval "before implementation", and the rule "Never rushed, never parallelized (§E serialization rule)." tools/check_merge_ready.py refuses to print a merge command for a pull request that changes any path matching `globs` unless its body carries exactly one `Architect-Audit: <path>` or `Owner-Waiver: YYYY-MM-DD` line that checks out at the pull request's head (T-154). For the audit line, 'checks out' has meant since T-155 (Owner decision, 2026-10-02) that the cited report ITSELF, as it is at that head, carries `Audited-PR: #N` naming this pull request and `Audited-Head: <40-hex>` naming the commit the auditor read; that this commit is the head or an ancestor of it; and that no path matching `globs` differs between that commit and the head. Until then any non-empty file under an AUDIT directory satisfied the line, including a round's report filed weeks earlier about another head. The same `globs` therefore decide two things: whether a pull request needs an audit, and what may not move after one. The row was written down for months and nothing refused a merge: #313, #314 and #321 went through without an audit on 2026-10-01/02, and the Owner's waiver for those three is on that row now.
derivation: `globs` is that file's `protected_roots`, each prefixed with `engine/` because the manifest is rooted at engine/ and a pull request's paths are rooted at the repository -- MINUS the roots named under `not_covered` with a `protected_root` key. It is derived and not invented so that the engine's own statement of its perimeter and this gate's cannot drift apart silently: tools/check_merge_ready.py::perimeter_drift compares the two every time the gate runs, and tools/test_check_merge_ready.py fails when the manifest gains or loses a root this file neither lists nor excludes with a reason. Matching is the engine's own (fnmatch, as engine/runtime/bro_workspace.py::matches_pattern), case-insensitively.

not_covered.reason: Tests are not security code. The engine protects them from a standard builder because CI gates on them; changing a test does not change what the wall, a lease, a gate or a signature does, so it does not need an Architect audit. A pull request that changes ONLY engine tests is therefore `not required` here. What this leaves open, stated: a test weakened so that a later change to the runtime passes is not caught by this gate -- the runtime change is.
Not a code path. No pull request can carry a change under a .git directory, so listing it would be a glob that can never match.

A secret-shaped NAME pattern, not a code path: it exists so the engine denies access to material that must never be in the tree at all. A committed secret is the supply-chain gate's finding (gitleaks), not an audit question.

A secret-shaped NAME pattern, not a code path. Stated honestly: a real source file whose NAME contains `secret` and that sits outside every listed root (for example under engine/docs/) is protected by the engine and is NOT audit-required here; one under engine/runtime/ or any other listed root is, by that root.
A secret-shaped NAME pattern, not a code path -- same reasoning and the same stated gap as `**/*secret*`.
A secret-shaped NAME pattern, not a code path -- same reasoning and the same stated gap as `**/*secret*`.

not_covered.what: roadmap §G.2's SECOND row -- "Trust-boundary / key / secret handling" -- which in practice is apps/desktop/src-tauri: the broker, the key manifest, provisioning, the launcher
not_covered.reason: NOT covered by this gate, and it carries the same mandatory audit. The roadmap delimits that row by subject, not by path, and a gate that guessed which Rust files are 'trust-boundary' would be inventing the Owner's rule for him. Recommended: the Owner names those paths on the row, and they are added here as a second declared list.

not_covered.what: roadmap §G.2's THIRD row outside engine/ -- contract and schema changes under bridge/ and the root contracts/
not_covered.reason: engine/schemas/** and engine/contracts/** ARE covered, because they are protected roots. bridge/ and the root contracts/ are outside the engine's manifest and outside the first row's words ("Any `engine/` security code"); that row asks for an audit before merge, not before implementation, and nothing here checks it.

not_covered.what: everything at the monorepo root that is security-relevant and is not under engine/: .github/workflows/**, tools/** (every check_*.py, including this gate), .claude/hooks/**, bridge/**
not_covered.reason: The engine's manifest is rooted at engine/ and says so in its own purpose string; the first row says `engine/`. These are outside both.

not_covered.what: engine/ paths outside every protected root: engine/docs/**, engine/AUDIT/**, engine/agents/*.md and the rest of the tree the manifest does not name
not_covered.reason: The gate follows the engine's own perimeter rather than a second opinion about it. If one of these should need an audit, the edit belongs in engine/config/protected-control-plane.json, and this file follows it.

not_covered.what: the cited audit's content, verdict and author, and whether anyone read the commit it names
not_covered.reason: The gate reads two lines of the report and asks git about the commit they name. That establishes that the report names this pull request and a commit in the history of the head that merges, and that the engine security content at that commit is the engine security content being merged. It does not establish that the report says GREEN, that an Architect and not the Builder wrote it, or that the named commit was read at all: `Audited-Head` is a claim made by whoever wrote the file. A program in the Builder's checkout cannot tell an Architect's file from a Builder's; a second principal who files or signs the report could, and nothing here is one.

not_covered.what: what moves after the audited commit OUTSIDE `globs`: engine tests, apps/desktop/src-tauri, tools/** and this gate
not_covered.reason: Between `Audited-Head` and the head only the paths that made the audit mandatory are held still. A test weakened after the audit, or trust-boundary code under the second row changed after it, passes; each is the same stated gap as its own entry above, seen from the audit's side.

A pull request that narrows this list is not audit-required by this list. What holds it instead: the drift test fails in CI when a protected root is neither listed nor excluded, and the set of excluded roots is pinned by a test, so a new exclusion is an edit to a test that names it.
